Element: requestIdleScroll() method

The requestIdleScroll() method of the Element interface schedules a smooth scroll that starts only when the browser has an idle period, so that the scroll does not compete with input handling or layout work.

It is useful for scrolling a log view or a chat panel after new content arrives, when the exact moment of the scroll does not matter.

Note: This page describes a fictional API used as a test fixture, and no browser implements it.

Syntax

requestIdleScroll()
requestIdleScroll(options)

Parameters

options Optional

An object with the following properties:

block

One of "start", "center", or "end". Defaults to "end", because most callers want to reveal the newest item.

timeout

A number of milliseconds after which the scroll happens even if no idle period has occurred. Defaults to 500.

Return value

A Promise that resolves once the scroll has finished, or rejects if the element was removed from the document before the scroll began.

Examples

const log = document.querySelector("#log");
log.append(entry);
log.lastElementChild.requestIdleScroll({ block: "end", timeout: 250 });

Specifications

This feature is not part of any specification.
